notes: Workflow-tool fan-out. Recipe targets 3 parallel children (a trivial task + `sleep 20` each); the spec hard-asserts only >=2 DISTINCT children both linked within a tight window of the same triggering turn (the schema has no native 'count N' or 'concurrently alive' primitive -- see metadata.json caveats -- so two new_session-constrained parent_linked phases anchored to the SAME parent_turn_start is the strongest concurrency proof the current phase-matching engine supports; it proves genuine fan-out rather than one-at-a-time sequential spawning). Session-birth follows the muse single-birth FilesUnderRoot pattern (2-1/3-1/3-2 precedent): anchored to start UNPINNED. child_a_linked/child_b_linked reuse 3-1's CONTAMINATION guard verbatim (min_delay_ms skips the earliest same-turn ambient skill-reminder/goal-reminder/verify-reminder child; record must cross-check the raw parent transcript's task_stream_linked entry for each matched child -- task_kind:workflow.agent.native (or an owner_kind:"workflow" record if the dedicated Workflow tool fired) with NO display.role:reminder tag -- a bare parent_linked match on task_kind alone is not sufficient, since 3.1's own assessment established task_kind:workflow.agent.native fires for EVERY native subagent unconditionally, not just fan-out children). fanout_working mirrors 3-1's intermediate_working: the parent holds working across both children's lifetime (duration_at_least_ms), with no phantom 'journal'/'unknown'-project session ever appearing (narrated only -- the invariants DSL has no 'no session named X' form). parent_turn_end mirrors 3-2's drained_ready: SubagentCount(parent) returning to 0 is implicit in the parent reaching its own final ready (cleanupParentChildrenOnReady), NOT a separate transcript_removed sweep event -- muse never deletes a completed child's session.jsonl from disk (unlike claude-code's journal.jsonl bug shape), so there is no file-removal event to assert here.

text: Parent session appears in ready shortly after the muse TUI finishes launching (single-birth, no presession split)
User opt-in prompt ('use a workflow to fan out 3 parallel agents...') drives parent ready → working

First fan-out child linked to the parent (ParentSessionID = parent.session_id, materialized under <parent>/subagent/<child-id>/session.jsonl). min_delay_ms skips the earliest same-turn ambient reminder child; record must confirm via the raw transcript this is a real fan-out child (task_kind:workflow.agent.native / owner_kind:workflow, no display.role:reminder tag)

A SECOND, DISTINCT child linked to the parent within the same short window after the triggering turn (new_session:true forces a session id never matched by an earlier phase, i.e. not child_a) — this is the machine-checkable proof of genuine concurrent fan-out rather than one child spawned at a time. Same contamination guard as child_a_linked applies.

invariants: no state_transition to ready for parent
no state_transition to waiting for parent
text: Parent stays working while the workflow children run (SubagentCount(parent) reflects the live count, recipe targets 3). No session ever surfaces that is attributable to a workflow bookkeeping/journal file — no phantom session, no 'unknown'-project session (narrated: the invariants DSL has no direct 'no session named X' form, so record/manual review confirms this against the raw recording).

Parent transitions working → ready only once every child has reported back and reached its own ready — with no other live children, cleanupParentChildrenOnReady drops them from the live count, so SubagentCount(parent) is back to 0 as soon as this phase lands (the SAME mechanism 3-2 background-subagent's drained_ready phase already exercises; there is no separate file-removal/sweep event to assert since muse never deletes a completed child's session.jsonl)
